title: Multi-region fallback playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a compact, user-facing and GTM-ready collection of messaging, incident narratives, and competitive notes focused on multi-region routing and graceful degradation (fallbacks). Its aimed at GTM (field, product marketing, sales engineering) and SRE/solutions-engineering partners who need concise, repeatable language for customer conversations and collateral.

Top-level positioning statement (single line):
When your application must stay responsive under real-world failures, Redwood Inference keeps requests running by routing across regions and degrading predictably — not silently — so developers can rely on continuity, cost predictability, and data controls.

Audience buckets (how to tailor):
- Product / Platform teams: focus on deterministic behavior, region pinning, and auditability.
- Customer-facing engineering: emphasize debug tooling, traces, and fallbacks that preserve semantics.
- Security / Compliance: highlight VPC/private control plane and region-level isolation options.
- Executives / procurement: emphasize uptime guarantees, measurable cost of failure mitigation, and SLAs.

Three short trust snippets (for emails / one-pagers):
- "We never route silently: when your primary region is impaired, Redwood switches to a pinned fallback and logs the change so you can audit user impact and respond."
- "Multi-region failover with policy controls: choose latency-first, cost-first, or data-bound routing and get predictable outcomes during incidents."
- "Fallbacks preserve behavior: automatic model variant downgrades are paired with quality checks and rollback hooks to prevent silent regressions."

Fallback flavours and when to call them out:
- Active-active cross-region: call out for global apps with tight latency SLAs. Highlight session affinity and KV-cache warming.
- Active-passive with fast failover: emphasize RTO metrics (ms to seconds) and audit trail.
- Model-variant fallback (smaller quantized model): emphasize deterministic quality degradation and cost savings.
- Regional data-bound fallback (stay in-region for data residency): describe how policy enforces no cross-border routing except for approved fallbacks.

Incident narrative templates (customer-facing) - three levels:
1) Short status update (for product dashboards / emails):
- Subject: "Service update: temporary routing change for inference in us-west-2"
- Body: "At 02:04 UTC we observed elevated error rates in us-west-2 due to a GPU kernel regression. Traffic for your routes was redirected to us-east-1 under your configured failover policy (latency-preferred). The active requests completed with a median latency increase of 28% while token costs remained within expected thresholds. No data left your VPC. Engineers applied a mitigant and normal routing resumed at 02:21 UTC. We logged the event under INCIDENT-2026-02-15-03 (link)."

2) Post-incident technical summary (for SEs and platform teams):
- Timeline with timestamps
- Root cause summary (kernel mismatch, autoscaler thrash, network flap)
- What changed for the customer (region switch, model rollback, degraded throughput)
- Impact matrix: availability, latency, cost delta, and quality regression measures (if any)
- Artifacts: traces, console links, debug commands we ran
- Next steps and compensations (if applicable)

3) Executive brief (for CSMs / leadership):
- One-sentence impact, duration, and customer segments affected
- Confidence level and postmortem ETA
- Customer-level mitigations (SLA credits, dedicated support)

Messaging dos and donts (tone and content):
- Do: be explicit about what changed and why; anchor statements in measurable metrics.
- Do: offer tangible next steps (e.g., change routing policy, enable proactive warmup, schedule a runbook review).
- Dont: bury failure modes in generic "latency spike" language.
- Dont: promise invisibility; promise predictability and auditability.

Competitive differentiation (callouts for conversations):
- Compared to hyperscaler managed endpoints: hyperscalers often hide routing and make region failover opaque. Redwood gives configurable routing policies, per-route metrics, and an audit trail so teams can reason about tradeoffs.
- Compared to DIY inference stacks: DIY can be cheaper at scale but lacks the unified control plane for rollouts, multi-region routing, and fast, production-grade fallbacks. Redwood bundles predictable failovers, rollout controls, and SRE playbooks.
- Compared to inference-specialist vendors who focus on single-site performance: Redwoods advantage is a consistent runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with the same multi-region behavior and operator tooling.

Objections and rebuttals (quick bullets):
- "We can replicate across regions ourselves": Rebuttal: replication isnt just about copies — its about deterministic request routing, cache warming, model variant parity, and operational playbooks; Redwood builds these into the control plane.
- "Failovers will increase cost": Rebuttal: Redwood surfaces cost delta estimates for failovers and supports cost-first routing to constrain spend; also, partial degradations (quantized model fallback) can reduce cost while preserving function.
- "We need strict data residency": Rebuttal: Redwood supports region pinning and policy-protected fallbacks; cross-border routing only happens under explicit, auditable rules.

Customer-facing quick scripts (SEs / SDRs):
- On discovery call: "How are you handling regional outages today? If your app needs deterministic behavior during an outage — i.e., a controlled fallback instead of a black-box retry — we can show a demo of our multi-region routing and model-variant fallback."
- In follow-up email: short bulleted benefits + invite to demo with routing policy editor screenshot.

Playbook for enabling a new customer on multi-region failover (ops checklist):
- Walkthrough routing policy: latency-first vs cost-first vs compliance-bound
- Capture expected latency band and critical routes (per-API endpoint)
- Configure warmup hooks for KV/prefix caching and pre-warm model weights in failover regions
- Define automatic quality checks (smoke prompts) and alert thresholds
- Agree on SLAs and scoreboard metrics to display in Console

SLOs and metrics customers want to see (recommended default):
- Failover RTO (median and 95p)
- Latency delta during failover (median, 95p)
- Error rate delta (percentage points)
- Model-quality drift score (automatic eval on smoke prompts)
- Cost delta per 1M tokens rerouted

Example quality-safe fallback policy (natural language for customers):
"If us-west-2 error rate > 5% for 2m AND avg latency > 700ms, route to us-east-1 using session-affinity. If model quality on smoke prompts drops > 8% on the fallback model, pause fallback and notify the SRE and the customer."

Incident handling play (SRE <-> SE choreography):
- Detect: Console alerts and synthetic smoke prompts trigger paging
- Contain: Activate pre-approved routing policy to an adjacent region; start cache-warm operations and model pre-loads
- Communicate: Send status update using the short status template within 10 minutes
- Repair: Fix root cause; roll back routing if stable for 15 minutes at baseline SLA metrics
- Review: Postmortem within 72 hours, customer-facing summary within 5 business days

Collateral ideas (quick):
- One-pager: "Predictable failovers: how Redwood keeps inference online"
- Interactive demo in Console: toggle routing policy and simulate regional outage
- Playbook webinar for SEs: run-throughs, objection handling, live postmortem demo

Action items (GTM owners):
- Product marketing: draft one-pager and email templates (owner: Aisha Patel)
- SE playbook: create a 15-minute demo script and console walkthrough (owner: Diego Ramirez)
- Solutions eng: prepare 2 reproducible demos for active-active and model-variant fallback (owner: Morgan O'Neill)
- Legal / compliance: finalize language for cross-border routing opt-in (owner: Priya Desai)

Notes / open questions (working):
- Should GRPC vs REST behavior during failover be called out separately? (ask serving-runtime)
- Add concrete cost numbers for common failover scenarios (follow up with finance)
- Consider a canned customer TCO slide for buy-side conversations

Raw snippets for collateral (copy-paste friendly):
- Headline: "When a region fails, your app shouldnt fall off a cliff. Redwood routes, degrades, and explains why."
- Subhead: "Predictable outcomes, auditable decisions, and fast recoveries across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- CTA: "See how failover behaves with your prompts — schedule a live failover drill."
